context.title: Palace, Pillars and Bronze Sea
context.summary: Solomon spends thirteen years on his palace. A craftsman named Hiram casts two great bronze pillars, a huge basin called the 'sea,' and ten wheeled stands for the temple.
context.background: The 'house of the forest of Lebanon' was named for its rows of cedar pillars; later it stored gold shields (10:17). The bronze-worker Hiram is not King Hiram but a craftsman whose mother was a widow of Naphtali and whose father was from Tyre.

customs.note: Names given to the two bronze pillars at the temple porch. Jachin likely means 'he establishes,' and Boaz 'in him is strength.'
A giant bronze basin on twelve bronze oxen. Chronicles says the priests washed in it (2 Chronicles 4:6).

watchFor: Compare thirteen years spent on the palace (v. 1) with seven on the temple (6:38).

people.name: Solomon
people.summary: Peaceful, (Heb. Shelomoh), David’s second son by Bathsheba, i.e., the first after their legal marriage (2 Sam. 12). He was probably born about B.C. 1035 (1 Chr. 22:5; 29:1).

people.name: Pharaoh
people.summary: The Pharaoh of the Exodus was probably Menephtah I., the fourteenth and eldest surviving son of Rameses II. He resided at Zoan, where he had the various interviews with Moses and Aaron recorded in the book of Exodus.

people.name: Hiram
people.summary: The “master workman” whom Hiram sent to Solomon. He was the son of a widow of Dan, and of a Tyrian father. In 2 Chr. 2:13 “Huram my father” should be Huram Abi, the word “Abi” (rendered here “my father”) being regarded as a proper name, or it may perhaps be a title of distinction given to Huram, and equivalent to “master.”

people.name: Naphtali
people.summary: My wrestling, the fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s handmaid (Gen. 30:8). When Jacob went down into Egypt, Naphtali had four sons (Gen. 46:24).

people.name: Boaz
people.summary: The husband of Ruth, a wealthy Bethlehemite. By the “levirate law” the duty devolved on him of marrying Ruth the Moabitess (Ruth 4:1-13).

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

places.name: Lebanon
places.summary: White, “the white mountain of Syria,” is the loftiest and most celebrated mountain range in Syria. It is a branch running southward from the Caucasus, and at its lower end forking into two parallel ranges, the eastern or Anti-Lebanon, and the western or Lebanon proper.

places.name: Tyre
places.summary: A rock, now es-Sur; an ancient Phoenician city, about 23 miles, in a direct line, north of Acre, and 20 south of Sidon. Sidon was the oldest Phoenician city, but Tyre had a longer and more illustrious history.

places.name: Jordan
places.summary: But besides these two historical fountains there is a third, called the Hasbany, which rises in the bottom of a valley at the western base of Hermon, 12 miles north of Tell-el-Kady.

places.name: Succoth
places.summary: A city on the east of Jordan, identified with Tell Dar’ala, a high mound, a mass of debris, in the plain north of Jabbok and about one mile from it (Josh. 13:27).

places.name: most holy place
places.summary: One of the two portions into which the tabernacle was divided (Ex. 26:31; 37:17-25; Heb. 9:2). It was 20 cubits long and 10 in height and breadth.

events.title: Construction of Solomon's Temple
events.summary: Passage: 1 Kings 5:1–7:51. Place: Jerusalem. Lasted about 7 years.

events.title: Reign of Solomon
events.summary: Passage: 1 Kings 2:12–11:42. People: Solomon. Place: Jerusalem. Lasted about 40 years.
